paper.title_en: Uncovering Hierarchical Sub-Population of Binary Black Holes
paper.abstract_en: The growing gravitational-wave census now contains 259 binary black hole systems with false-alarm rates below $1~{\rm yr}^{-1}$, enabling studies of trends, structure, and subpopulations that may reveal their formation mechanisms. We test whether hierarchical interpretations of previously proposed mass structure are consistent with the observed spins. We construct a multi-component mixture model in which each component has independently inferred merger-rate, mass, spin-magnitude, and spin-orientation distributions, while all components share a common redshift distribution. The model combines a power law with five Gaussian mass components whose ordered prior ranges reduce parameter degeneracies. We recover overall mass and redshift distributions consistent with published results, as well as the previously identified trend toward low, preferentially aligned spins at low masses and larger, isotropically oriented spins at high masses. However, unlike some previous analyses, we find that every Gaussian component except the lowest-mass component is consistent with isotropic spin orientations. Conditional on the adopted mass hierarchy, the inferred spins do not follow the mass--spin correlations expected from hierarchical mergers without additional spin evolution. Reconciling both distributions may therefore require additional physics. We present an illustrative, finely tuned spin-down model that could reconcile a hierarchical interpretation of much of the mass structure with the observed spin distribution.
